flashcards.q: What is a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) and what did it replace?
flashcards.a: A diffusion model whose backbone is a ViT-style transformer over VAE-latent patches instead of a convolutional U-Net. Introduced by Peebles & Xie (2022); the ancestor of Sora, SD3, and FLUX.

flashcards.q: State the two headline DiT results that demonstrated superiority over U-Nets.
flashcards.a: (1) Monotonic scaling: across 12 configurations, higher forward-pass Gflops consistently gave lower FID — legible scaling U-Nets lacked. (2) Efficiency: DiT-XL/2 reached FID 2.27 on ImageNet 256x256 at 119 Gflops vs ADM-U's 742 Gflops; at 512², 3.04 FID at 525 vs ADM-U's 3.85 at 2,813 Gflops (~5x efficiency).

flashcards.q: What is adaLN-Zero and why did it matter more than attention in DiT?
flashcards.a: The conditioning mechanism: timestep/label embeddings regress per-block scale-shift-gate parameters applied at every LayerNorm, with gates zero-initialized so each block starts as identity. Ablations showed this conditioning design drove the FID gains — identical transformers with cross-attention or in-context conditioning were dramatically worse.

flashcards.q: What is DiT's 'model compute beats sampling compute' lesson, with numbers?
flashcards.a: DiT-L/2 sampled at 1000 steps (80.7 Tflops/image) produced WORSE FID than DiT-XL/2 at just 128 steps (15.2 Tflops): 23.7 vs 25.9. Scaling inference steps cannot compensate for a limited backbone — quality problems are usually capacity/data problems.

flashcards.q: Define flow matching's training objective (CFM loss).
flashcards.a: Sample noise x0 and data x1, form the straight-line interpolation x_t=(1-t)x0+t*x1, and train v(x_t,t) to predict the constant velocity x1-x0 with plain MSE. Sampling integrates dx/dt=v with Euler steps of the resulting deterministic ODE.

flashcards.q: Why can flow-matching ODEs sample in ~10 steps where DDPM needs 50-1000?
flashcards.a: Near-straight linear-interpolation paths tolerate large Euler steps while staying close to the data manifold, unlike DDPM's curved stochastic paths. Rectified flow further straightens trajectories via re-pairing (~2 rounds), enabling 1-4 step sampling — the engine behind SD3 and FLUX. Practical speedups: 10-100x.

flashcards.q: What does rectified flow do, and which systems use it?
flashcards.a: Iteratively re-pairs (noise, data) samples by running the trained model to generate new pairs, then retrains — each round reduces trajectory curvature until paths are nearly straight and single Euler steps suffice. Stable Diffusion 3 ('Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers') and FLUX are built on it.

flashcards.q: State the consistency-model boundary condition and what it enables.
flashcards.a: f(x_t,t)=f(x0,0): the same function applied to any point on a probability-flow trajectory must return the endpoint. This lets sampling jump noise-to-data in one evaluation or 2-4 steps, trained by consistency distillation from a pretrained teacher or from scratch (sCM).

flashcards.q: Quote VideoLCM's measured speedup and its configuration details.
flashcards.a: On an A100 generating eight videos at 16x256x256: DDIM 50-step took 60s, VideoLCM 4-step took 10s (~6x cut; 104s to 16s at 16x448x256). The teacher's CFG weight was frozen at 9.0 during student training; guidance isn't needed at student inference. 2-4 steps suffice with structural priors like depth conditioning.

flashcards.q: What exactly degrades below ~4 sampling steps in distilled models?
flashcards.a: Blur and visible artifacts (fine detail and text rendering degrade first), plus mode-seeking behavior in one-step students that loses diversity/tail fidelity versus the teacher. The cause: coarse integration turns latent-space regression into mean-prediction across modes. Adversarial distillation (SDXL-Turbo's ADD: student+teacher+discriminator) recovers sharpness with GAN-style instability.

flashcards.q: What is Perceptual Flow Matching (PFM) and what did it show in 2026?
flashcards.a: Supervising flow matching in a pretrained perceptual feature space instead of VAE latent space shifts the regression minimizer from mean-seeking to mode-seeking. Result: 35-50 sampling steps cut to 4-8 without any teacher model; COCO 8-step FID 33.93 / CLIP 31.70 (SOTA among 8-step methods). Limit: still degrades below two steps.

flashcards.q: How do spacetime patches bring video into DiT?
flashcards.a: Sora packs the compressed spatiotemporal latent volume into patches spanning space AND time, embedded as tokens for one standard transformer — handling variable resolutions, durations, aspect ratios with no per-format architecture. Video generation becomes a token-scaling problem; cost scales as steps x tokens.

flashcards.q: Give the video-generation cost model and the ranked cost-reduction levers.
flashcards.a: Cost scales with steps x tokens, where tokens grow linearly with frames x area divided by VAE compression. Levers ranked: consistency-distilled step counts (biggest multiplier), duration/resolution ladders with draft-then-refine, stronger temporal VAE compression, then batching/caching serving mechanics.

flashcards.q: When are U-Net/conv designs still the right choice over DiT?
flashcards.a: Small datasets (conv sample-efficiency beats transformer scaling headroom that never activates), ultra-low-latency high-res pixel work, edge/memory-constrained devices, and precise local editing tasks. Modern practice hybrids conv frontends with transformer middles. At frontier pretraining scale, DiT's legible scaling wins.

flashcards.q: What does classifier-free guidance (CFG) do, and how do distilled models change its usage?
flashcards.a: CFG extrapolates away from unconditional predictions (v = v_uncond + w(v_cond - v_uncond), w typically 3-9) to sharpen prompt adherence at the cost of double forward passes. Distilled students have guidance baked in (LCM froze teacher CFG at 9.0), so post-hoc guidance tuning disappears — oversaturated/burnt outputs on such checkpoints mean switching tiers, not turning a knob.
